rv.q: Here's a charming, simple, slightly baggy staging of Louis de Bernières's 1994 bestseller.
Melly Still’s astute and assured direction, has resulted in a captivating evenings entertainment and most importantly, one which is a credit to the source material.
The theatrical knowhow on abundant display amplifies one's disappointment in a gatheringly soapy text.
But there's an over-arching earnestness to the storytelling that left me largely unmoved and uninvolved.

cn.t: Melly Still's adaptation receives mixed reviews, with critics praising its inventive stagecraft and physical storytelling but finding it uneven. The production proves charming yet baggy, working better as a showcase for Still's directorial style than as a faithful adaptation.
